title: Multifractal Magnons Around Localized Defects
authors: Adarsh Hullahalli, Yusuf Khand, Christos Panagopoulos, Christina Psaroudaki
abstract: Multifractal wavefunctions fluctuate over a hierarchy of spatial scales, remaining spatially extended while exhibiting strongly nonuniform structure. We show that magnons in otherwise crystalline two-dimensional magnets can exhibit such behavior on mesoscopic scales, without disorder or quasiperiodicity. A localized defect can mix discrete groups of nearly degenerate magnon states in a finite sample, generating multiscale interference patterns and multifractal wavefunctions. We demonstrate this mechanism for both a simple spin defect and topological magnetic skyrmions. Large-scale spin-wave calculations for skyrmions in chiral and frustrated magnets reveal clear multifractal diagnostics over the full accessible range of system sizes of above-gap modes. Crucially, skyrmions make these states experimentally observable by hybridizing them with magnetically active internal deformation modes, which gives a subset of the multifractal states a nonzero magnetic dipole moment. These states can therefore be excited by uniform ac fields and remain distinguishable at realistic frequency resolution, providing a direct route to observing mesoscopic magnon multifractality.
summary: This work demonstrates that localized defects, such as magnetic skyrmions, can induce multifractal behavior in magnon wavefunctions within otherwise ordered 2D magnets. By analyzing the scaling properties of these wavefunctions, the authors provide a theoretical framework and a pathway to experimentally observe this mesoscopic quantum phenomenon using uniform AC fields.
main_problem: To determine if magnons in crystalline 2D magnets, without disorder or quasiperiodicity, can exhibit multifractal wavefunctions on mesoscopic scales.
main_result: Localized defects, such as point defects or magnetic skyrmions, can generate measurable multifractal structure in above-gap magnon modes, providing a direct, observable route to study mesoscopic magnon multifractality.
method: The study employs multifractal analysis techniques, calculating generalized dimensions ($	au(q)$, $D_q$) from the scaling of probability moments of the magnon wavefunctions.
model_or_system: The system models magnons (spin-wave excitations) in ordered 2D magnets, specifically investigating the effects of localized defects or topological magnetic skyrmions on the magnon eigenmodes.
key_observables:

important_parameters: Mesoscopic scales, defect strength, system size ($L$), and frequency resolution ($\delta\omega$).
main_assumptions: The observed multifractality is mesoscopic and does not persist in the strict thermodynamic limit; the analysis relies on specific definitions of current coupling and multifractal thresholds.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the generation of multifractal patterns via defect coupling, show diagnostic plots ($	au(q)$, $D_q$) confirming non-linear scaling, and demonstrate the measurable signatures in transport observables.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical possibility of multifractality via defects, demonstrating this using both simple defects and skyrmions, and finally quantifying the signatures in transport properties by splitting coupling into multifractal and extended components.
why_interesting: The connection between topological defects (skyrmions) and measurable quantum wave function statistics (multifractality) provides a novel diagnostic tool for characterizing complex many-body excitations in magnetic materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Shell Structure and Multifractal Interference Patterns. (a) First ∼1700 energy level degeneracies for a chiral magnet-type dispersion. (b) Fourier components ∆Sµ (gray dots) generated from coherent interference of states Sµ (red dots) within a chosen high- degeneracy shell (Ω= 48). (c) Multifractal patterns generated by an equal-phase superposition of red states, characteristic of a defect- hybridized magnon state. (d)-(f) nonlinear τ(q), q-dependent gen- eralized dimensions Dq with D1 < D0, and finite-width singularity spectrum (α, f(α)) confirming multifractality of the wavefunction.

FIG. 2. Multifractal Magnons around Local Defects. Selected multifractal modes around local defects calculated on a 1200 × 1200 lattice, and corresponding metrics confirming multifractality. (a) Probability density of a magnon wavefunction found around an S = 0 spin defect. (b)-(e) Respectively, nonlinear τ(q) curve, q-dependent generalized dimensions with D1 < D0, finite-width singularity spectrum with α(0) > D0, and reciprocal space support. (f)-(j) Analogous plots around a chiral skyrmion. (k)-(o) Analogous plots around a frustrated skyrmion, indicating present but weaker multifractality due to a competing single-scale hybridization channel (see the high-intensity ring with radius ∼|K|/3...

FIG. 4. System Size and Skyrmion Number Dependence. (a) Information dimension D1 and (b) correlation dimension D2, av- eraged over 100 chiral magnon modes, versus linear system size L. Each curve corresponds to a fixed number Nsk of randomly posi- tioned skyrmions. Both dimensions remain below the extended limit D1 = D2 = 2 over mesoscopic sizes.

FIG. 3. Multifractal Statistics. Scatterplots of ∆α and D1 of the 100 modes nearest to different energy targets around a single chiral skyrmion (a) and a single frustrated skyrmion (b), illustrating how the distribution of multifractal signatures depends on the scattering regime. Frustrated modes are statistically closer to the extended limit of D1 = 2 and ∆α = 0 due to competing single-scale hybridization. Red triangles in both plots correspond to modes displayed in Fig. 2. FIG. 5. Observable Multifractal Magnons. Longitudinal dipole spectral weight W z(ω) and dipole-weighted information dimension D z 1 (ω) for the full magnon spectrum of a 120 × 120 chiral system, with frequency resolution δω = 0.05. Windows with finite W z and D z 1 < 2 identify spectral windows populated by magnetically acces- sible multifractal modes.
